key_insight: A DSL-guided multi-agent LLM framework turns natural-language materials rules into symbolic predicates, helping the model reason more reliably for inverse design of double perovskite oxides.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical path for faster, more interpretable materials discovery using LLM agents without requiring large task-specific training datasets.
method: Translate design rules into chemistry DSL predicates
Use predicates to query accumulated materials data for statistical evidence
Iteratively refine rules and candidates in a multi-agent ORCHESTRA design loop
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that symbolic predicates helped identify unsupported rules, validate new rules, and improve the rule store across iterative cycles, with better performance than natural-language-only rules on harder target properties.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the predefined DSL and accumulated materials data, so weak rule encoding or sparse evidence could limit gains.
paper_title: Symbolic Predicate-Guided Language Agents for Inverse Design of Perovskite Oxides
